description: On display in the Therese Angelo Wing. Manufacturer's no. 6786. One of 18 MB-339CBs flown by No. 14 Squadron RNZAF 1991-2001. Museum aircraft page checked September 2026.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Built at the Airspeed factory Portsmouth in 1945. Restored and on public display in the Aircraft Hall since February 2016. Carried civil registration G-AIKR.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Built at Rearsby England November 1950 as RAF WE563. Allocated to the Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition 1955. On display in the Aircraft Hall.
aliases: Auster T7; T7; WE563; Auster Mk 7c
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Oldest surviving fully intact RNZAF aircraft and the last Avro 626 in existence. British Air Ministry no. 811. On display in the Aircraft Hall.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Composite airframe rebuilt at Wigram in the 1980s; fuselage largely NZ415 (LT376) with parts of NZ410 NZ422 and VL352. Displayed as type example NZ406 of the School of General Reconnaissance RNZAF Bell Block 1943. Stored in the Reserve Collection.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Manufacturer's no. 343. Stored in the Reserve Collection and viewable on the daily tour.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Manufacturer's no. 6518. Suspended on display in the Therese Angelo Wing. One of six Bell 47G-3B-1 purchased for the RNZAF in 1965. Wikipedia gives this airframe as NZ3705; the museum's own page states NZ3706.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: United States Army airframe 69-15923 displayed as the generic RNZAF type example 'NZ3800'. Manufacturer's no. AAB 12211. In storage in No. 2 Hangar.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Manufacturer's no. 4812. On display in the Aircraft Hall.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Full-scale replica of Britannia, New Zealand's first military aircraft, presented in 1913 by the Imperial Air Fleet Committee. Built by David Comrie. On display in the Atrium.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Nose and forward cabin section plus an engine and main undercarriage of RNZAF Boeing 727-100C NZ7272, the only survivor of the RNZAF fleet. Built by Boeing in 1968 for United Airlines, sold to the RNZAF 1981, retired August 2003 with 46216 hours. Acquired 2019.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: On display in the Therese Angelo Wing. One of 12 Freighters operated by the RNZAF from 1951, largely with No. 41 Squadron in South-East Asia.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: USAF forward air control aircraft on long-term loan from the National Museum of the United States Air Force since 1990. Displayed in FAC configuration. Currently stored in No. 2 Hangar.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Consolidated Catalina OA-10A built in Canada by Canadian Vickers; never served with the RNZAF. Recovered damaged from New Guinea in 1975, restoration by RNZAF volunteers from 1983, transferred to Wigram 1990. Partially restored as a type representative.
aliases: Catalina; PBV1A; PBY; OA-10A; OA10A; PBV
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: USAAF airframe 41-14205 displayed as RNZAF NZ3000 in the Aircraft Hall. The museum's page calls it a P-40E; Wikipedia lists it as a P-40F.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Built 1957, operated in Australia as VH-AAL, to New Zealand September 1965 for aerial topdressing, presented to the museum by Fieldair in 1985 as a type example. Displayed as NZ6001, the RNZAF Trans-Antarctic Expedition Beaver lost on the Beardmore Glacier in 1960. Stored in the Reserve Collection.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Ex-RAF WA311, RNZAF instructional airframe INST193. Currently in storage in No. 2 Hangar.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Ex-RAF XH317, manufacturer's no. 15691, RNZAF instructional airframe INST205. On display in the Reserve Collection and viewable on the daily tour.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: One of the initial order of 10 RNZAF Devons, flown out from Britain arriving Wigram March 1952. Served with the Air Navigation School at Wigram until 1980. Stored in the Reserve Collection.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: New Zealand built, manufacturer's no. DHNZ 161. Displayed as NZ825 in the Therese Angelo Wing.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Ex-USAAF 45-960, manufacturer's no. 16963. On display in the Aircraft Hall.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Australian-built GAF Canberra B.20 wearing its RAAF serial A84-240. Manufacturer's no. GAF.C.FF40. Currently in storage in No. 2 Hangar.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Manufacturer's no. 5219. On display in the Aircraft Hall. The RNZAF received 48 Avengers in 1943-44 for Nos. 30 and 31 Squadrons.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Sole surviving RNZAF Andover; served only with No. 42 Squadron, flown to Wigram June 1996. Moved into the reserve collection area of the Therese Angelo Wing in December 2022.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Manufacturer's no. 236. One of four SH-2F Seasprites jointly operated by the RNZN and RNZAF 1997-2001. Stored in the Reserve Collection.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: First of the RNZAF's five C-130H Hercules, delivered April 1965 and retired 2025. Arrived at the museum February 2025; a new extension to house it and the Orion was approved by Christchurch City Council in June 2025.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Ex-RAF V9241, manufacturer's no. 3826. On display in the Aircraft Hall.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Retired RNZAF maritime patrol Orion held at the museum; shown to the public on Orion open days pending completion of a new display building.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: In storage in No. 2 Hangar. The museum page gives manufacturer's no. 14097 for both NZ6205 and NZ6254, which cannot both be correct.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Ex-US Navy A-4L 149516 held on loan and painted as RNZAF NZ6207; the real NZ6207 crashed near Bulls on 18 October 1974. Recorded here on the strength of adf-serials and the Skyhawk Association; the museum's own 2026 aircraft index no longer lists it, so its present status is unconfirmed.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Two-seat trainer variant. In storage in No. 2 Hangar.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Ex-RAF EZ331, manufacturer's no. 88-16326. Displayed as NZ948 in the Aircraft Hall.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Built 1944 for the USAAF, converted to Cavalier standard 1967 and supplied to the Indonesian Air Force as F-367 in 1972. Acquired by the museum in 1985 in exchange for a Vampire T.11 and rebuilt at Ohakea to P-51D standard. Displayed as NZ2410 of No. 4 (TAF) Squadron. Manufacturer's no. 122-41367.
aliases: Mustang; NZ2410; F-367; P51D; P51; F367
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Final CT/4B built for the RNZAF, manufactured in Hamilton and entering service at Wigram 28 August 1978. Manufacturer's no. 096. Flown in to the museum in 2000. Stored in the Reserve Collection.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: American copy of the German Fieseler Fi 103 (V-1), on long-term loan from the Smithsonian Institution. Transferred from MOTAT in Auckland to the Air Force Museum.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Construction no. 392/38. Arrived in New Zealand 1958 for the Tauranga Gliding Club, later Waipukurau Gliding Club, then No. 11 Squadron Air Training Corps from 1975. One of only four Ka 4s on public display worldwide. Stored in the Reserve Collection.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Replica built in England 1978-1983 by Skysport Engineering with an original Le Rhone rotary engine; crashed on its first flight in July 1986 and acquired by the museum in 1995 for static restoration. Displayed as N6460 of No. 3 (Naval) Squadron RNAS flown by New Zealander Harold Beamish. On display in the Caldwell Gallery.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Built at Castle Bromwich; manufacturer's no. 11892. Displayed as OU-V of No. 485 (NZ) Squadron RAF 1945, in the Aircraft Hall.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Built at Weybridge and shipped to New Zealand March 1935. Served with the Bomber Reconnaissance Flight, No. 2 FTS Woodbourne and No. 1 (GR) Squadron; broken up at Ohakea 14 June 1944 and later recovered. Under restoration in the Conservation Workshops using parts of NZ124 NZ105 NZ355 and NZ357; viewable on the daily tour.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

description: Entered Royal Navy service 1964, sold to the RNZN July 1982 and retired 1995. Donated to the museum by Westland Helicopters in 1998. On display in the Therese Angelo Wing.
museum_name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand
